scope: Round-3 changed stories (61, from 07_validation/reports/changed_in_round3.json) plus the previous and next story in each of their arcs (83 neighbours): 144 stories, days -5 to 117, read in full in day order. Focus: port-condition timeline (X-Ray Sat. Sept. 11, Yankee Sun. Sept. 12, Zulu Mon. Sept. 13, return to anchorage Sept. 17, partial reopening Oct. 14), FBI searches moved to Mon. Dec. 27, days 102-103, dates/weekdays/durations, canon, continuity, word counts, grammar, Coast Guard realism, hidden links. Dataset-wide greps for Saturday/Sept. 11 closures, ships riding out the storm at anchor and search mentions on days 100-103.

findings.old: X-Ray is the first of the storm port conditions.
findings.new: X-Ray is one step in a graduated series of storm port conditions.
findings.reason: Real-world error: Coast Guard hurricane port conditions begin with Whiskey (gale-force winds within 72 hours); X-Ray (48 hours) is the second. Rewording avoids implying a Whiskey setting that is not in the public record.

findings.old: Here is what the Coast Guard's first storm condition means
findings.new: Here is what the Coast Guard's storm condition means
findings.reason: Same port-condition realism point as M003-01: X-Ray is not the first condition in the Coast Guard's sequence (Whiskey precedes it).

findings.old: By Zulu, every vessel should already be where it intends to ride out the weather.
findings.new: By Zulu, the channel is shut, and anything still at anchor should be heading for sea room.
findings.reason: Ruiz quote contradicts the story's own Sept. 13 entry and PUB-108: ships at the offshore anchorage put to sea under Zulu, so they were not already where they would ride out the storm.

findings.old: first postponed in September, days before Hurricane Rafael's landfall.
findings.new: first postponed on Sept. 11, three days before Hurricane Rafael's landfall.
findings.reason: Body is 298 words, below Continental Wire's 300-400 range; the exact postponement date (PUB-020, Sat. Sept. 11) adds two words and precision.

findings.old: 14 vessels had queued offshore when the channel first closed.
findings.new: 14 vessels had queued offshore when the port closed to inbound traffic.
findings.reason: Imprecise: the 14 vessels were at the anchorage at the Sept. 12 inbound closure (PUB-107); when the channel closed to all traffic Sept. 13 they put to sea (PUB-108).

findings.old: "Every week we move more of the queue,"
findings.new: "Every day we move more of the queue,"
findings.reason: The partial reopening was only three days earlier (Thursday, Oct. 14); 'every week' does not fit.

findings.old: aboard MV Gulf Provider berthed about a month late
findings.new: aboard MV Gulf Provider came ashore about a month late
findings.reason: Containers do not berth; the ship berthed and the containers came ashore (PUB-059).

findings.old: through the port this late summer.
findings.new: through the port in late summer.
findings.reason: Awkward phrasing ('this late summer'); matches PUB-007 wording.

findings.old: "Corpus Christi had a month to recover from one shock," she said. "It got two weeks."
findings.new: "Corpus Christi spent a month shut by one shock," she said. "It got two weeks of traffic before the next."
findings.reason: Quote logic is muddled: the port was closed about a month after Rafael, then had two weeks of partial traffic before the blast; as written it says it 'had a month to recover' and then 'got two weeks'.
